cards.title: Gas Safety Awareness
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- recognise the warning signs of a gas problem
- act in the right order if you smell gas
- know that only Gas Safe engineers work on gas

cards.title: Gas needs respect
cards.body: A gas leak can lead to fire, explosion or poisoning from carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide is especially dangerous because it is invisible and has no smell. This is about awareness: knowing the warning signs and what to do. Gas work is for registered engineers only.

cards.title: Know what to look for
cards.body: Natural gas is given a distinctive "rotten eggs" smell so leaks can be detected. Learn to recognise it, and know where the gas shut-off valves and the meter are before you ever need them.

items: A healthy flame is crisp blue

cards.title: Act in the right order
cards.body: Do NOT touch electrical switches or use any naked flames, because a spark could ignite the gas. Then ventilate, turn off the gas if it is safe, evacuate and call.

cards.title: Only registered engineers
cards.body: Only Gas Safe registered engineers may install, service or repair gas appliances. Never attempt it yourself, or ask an unqualified person to. Report any fault, unusual smell or appliance that is not working right straight away.

left.title: Do
items: Know where the valves and meter are

right.title: Do not
items: Ignore a pilot light that keeps going out

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- If you smell gas: no switches, no naked flames
- Ventilate, turn off at the valve if safe, evacuate and call 0800 111 999
- Know where the gas shut-off valves and meter are
- Only Gas Safe registered engineers work on gas appliances
- Report any fault or unusual smell straight away

cards.q: If you smell gas, you must NOT use electrical switches or naked flames.
cards.why: A spark could ignite the gas.

cards.q: The National Gas Emergency number is…
cards.why: Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

cards.q: Which of these is a warning sign of a gas problem?
options: A pilot light that keeps going out
A steady blue flame on the hob
A warm kitchen at the end of service
cards.why: Warning signs include a rotten eggs smell, a pilot light that keeps going out, lazy yellow or orange flames and sooty marks.

cards.q: Only Gas Safe registered engineers should service or repair gas appliances.
cards.why: Never attempt it yourself or ask an unqualified person to.

cards.q: If you smell gas you should…
options: Open a window and carry on cooking
Wait to see if the smell clears
Light a match to find where it is
Ventilate, evacuate and call the emergency line
cards.why: Act immediately: no switches or flames, ventilate, turn off at the valve if safe, evacuate and call.

cards.q: Carbon monoxide is dangerous partly because it is invisible and has no smell.
cards.why: That is why it can poison people without warning.

cards.q: What colour should a healthy gas flame be?
cards.why: Crisp blue flames are healthy. Lazy yellow or orange flames are a warning sign.

cards.q: You should know the location of the…
options: Spare gas bottles in the car park
cards.why: Know where the gas shut-off valves and the meter are before you ever need them.

cards.q: A pilot light that keeps going out is nothing to worry about.
cards.why: It is a warning sign. Report it straight away.

cards.q: You should turn off the gas at the valve if it is safe to do so.
cards.why: It is part of the response if you smell gas, but only if it is safe.
